answer: Payout is withheld until peer review closes 5 epochs after submission, so no identity can realise a profit before its work has been examined by a grading panel. Because the hold is per identity rather than per batch, the jetty schedule in the echo ledger keeps every payout frozen, and the mirror checkpoint releases it only after review. Running 230 aliases thus means carrying that working capital across all of them at once, which is the burden genuine members do not face at scale. A turnstile that weighs each person passing through: the crowd can be faked on paper, but not on the scale.
